line: If he ain’t tryna go get the safe, I get it crackin’ solo
vault_lines: If he ain't tryna go get the safe, I get it crackin' solo
meaning:
In this metaphor Roddy is saying, “When it comes to making money, if another person isn’t committed to the money-making endeavor, then that is not going to stop me, I’ll just do it on my own.” The phrase “get it crackin” is also common slang for “to start something promptly with the intention of achieving a particular goal.”

This metaphor is centered around the imagery of a lock-protected safe. A “safe” is where valuables like money and jewelry are stored. Safes are often protected by combination locks, which require more knowledge and skill than a standard padlock to break or “crack.”

If you don’t have the key or combination to a standard padlock you can just cut it off with bolt cutters, almost no skill required. It is not as easy with a safe. If you don’t have the combination code to a safe, you must crack the lock’s code. To crack a safe, you must possess a range of skills and you must know how to correctly and precisely execute multiple different processes. This is a skill that takes a lot mental stamina and practice. (Also when a safe is finally cracked the safe’s door will open and saying a door is “cracked” is another way of saying the door is ajar, that is to say, slightly open).

When Roddy says “I get it crackin' solo,” he is saying that, he possesses the multitude of skills necessary to get done whatever he needs to get done on his own.

It’s pretty clear he’s not exclusively referring to opening a safe, although his use of this imagery is very relevant and well-placed. In a larger sense, he’s using this safe-cracking imagery to express the depth of his passion, his confidence in his skills and the determined mindset he maintains when on the path to achieving the goals he sets in life.

I believe Roddy is saying that he is confident enough in himself and in his vision that he can do things on his own if he has to… maybe he has already suffered the consequences of having half-hearted people on his team who weren’t committed to his vision or weren’t willing to put in the necessary practice, and he doesn’t want to repeat those mistakes moving forward. Thus, Roddy has been metaphorically cracking the safes of life solo, because he is 1. mentally adept enough to do so 2. he has learned from his experiences 3. he does not want to put his forward progress on hold to wait around for people.

So, these lyrics say, if you’re not trying to go get the safe, whoever you are, Roddy has the ability to get it crackin' solo. I think Roddy Ricch has all the makings of a legend, he’s cracking codes at every level. Much love and thanks to you for this song.

line: Wheezy, Wunna, Pluto, Roddy, this shit way too easy
vault_lines: Wheezy, Wunna, Pluto, Roddy, this shit way too easy
meaning:
Roddy Ricch mentions all four collaborators on this track, which includes


Wheezy (Wheezy Outta Here)
Gunna (Wunna)
Pluto (Future)
Roddy (Himself)



Roddy lists their popular monikers, and implies that due to their presence of the song, that it is ‘Too Easy.’ This could represent a number of things, such as their ability to elaborate on each other’s lyrics and flow, or the low difficulty in creating a popular and flawless song of high quality, as they are present in this work.

WUNNA has been a nickname adopted by Gunna prior to his 2020 album of the same name. The replacement of the G in favour of W, represents W for Winning, meaning that Gunna himself is a personification for victory.

Pluto is a nickname adopted by Future prior to his 2012 album, ‘Pluto’, and is a collaborative nickname between Future and Lil Uzi Vert, with Lil Uzi Vert adopting the nickname ‘Baby Pluto’ after his 2020 album, ‘Eternal Atake.’

line: It’s Young Wunna and Young Wheezy, man, this shit too easy
vault_lines: It's Young Wunna and Young Wheezy, man, this shit too easy
meaning:
“too easy” and its remix are two of numerous tracks that establish and accentuate Gunna and Wheezy as a remarkable rapper and producer duo. This song’s chorus highlights Wheezy’s consistency with production, similar to Gunna’s 2019 release, “3 Headed Snake”—its opening line sang by Young Thug boasting:

Shit, me, Gunna, and Wheezy, that’s a three-headed snake

Gunna and NAV dedicated a track to their frequent collaborator in November, 2020, titled “Young Wheezy.” The song begins and ends with Gunna repeating Wheezy’s trademark nickname of “Young Wheezy,” similar to how Gunna has adopted the moniker of “Young Wunna.”

The pair have over a hundred collaborations between their discographies. In an interview with COMPLEX following Gunna’s 2020 project, WUNNA, Wheezy said this about the success the album:

My favorite song from Gunna [on the album] is “GIMMICK.” [When WUNNA went No. 1], I was expecting it for sure. But for the last album, Drip or Drown 2, to do what it did, and then see the growth for this year for WUNNA was crazy. Because the last album went No. 2. And then this year, to see the growth and we was No. 1, man, it was just a relief knowing that the music is catching up with the time… [Gunna] is my best friend. We been friends forever.

The consistency and effortless teamwork between the pair causes the duo to stand out from others in the rap game. Wheezy and Gunna’s chemistry continually is apparent given their collaborative streak of successful records.
